name: LangChain
tagline: LangChain describes itself as the agent engineering platform
description: LangChain describes itself as the agent engineering platform. Open-source software; the repository lists the licence as MIT.
features: Open-source framework for building agents and LLM applications
Part of the LangChain ecosystem alongside LangGraph and LangSmith
useCases: Connecting models to tools and data
strengths: Source code and licence are public in the official repository
No licence fee for the software itself
limitations: You run and maintain it yourself, so hosting, hardware and support costs are your own
We have not run or benchmarked it

openSource.note: The official repository lists the licence as MIT

free.details: The software is free to use under its MIT licence; infrastructure and any hosted offerings are separate.

plans.name: Self-hosted (open source)
plans.note: Free software under the MIT licence; your own hosting and hardware costs apply

pricing.regional: No vendor price list. Any hosted or commercial offering from the same team is priced separately and is not covered here.

verification.notes: Project active. The repository page describes it as 'The agent engineering platform' and shows the MIT license. No pricing: open-source software; hosted LangSmith is a separate product.
verification.method: Opened in the Claude desktop built-in browser; page text read

profile.headline: An open-source framework for starting agents with any model provider

capabilities.title: Start an agent quickly
capabilities.text: LangChain is the quick-start framework: begin from templates with any model provider.

capabilities.title: Use proven patterns or customise them
capabilities.text: Build with established agent patterns, or tailor them.

capabilities.title: Keep control of the pieces
capabilities.text: You choose your own harness, context, memory and model.

capabilities.title: Grow into the rest of the stack
capabilities.text: Move to langgraph for low-level control or deepagents for long-running work.

featureCards.name: Any model provider
featureCards.text: The framework is described as working with any model provider.

featureCards.name: Templates
featureCards.text: Quick starts for common agent shapes.

featureCards.name: deepagents
featureCards.text: A sibling framework for long-running agents on complex tasks.

featureCards.name: langgraph
featureCards.text: A sibling framework for agents with low-level control.

featureCards.name: LangSmith
featureCards.text: The paid platform for observing, evaluating and deploying agents built with these frameworks.

featureCards.name: Docs and Academy
featureCards.text: Documentation at docs.langchain.com and the LangChain Academy courses.

audienceDetail.text: Developers who want a fast route from idea to a working agent.
Teams that need to own their harness, memory and model choice.
The company cites large customers for its wider platform.

scenarios.title: Build a support assistant
scenarios.text: A customer story on the site describes an assistant that cut case resolution time substantially.

scenarios.title: Automate order processing
scenarios.text: Another customer story reports thousands of orders handled automatically each day.

scenarios.title: Orchestrate agents across stages
scenarios.text: A third describes coordinating agents across several customer stages.

gettingStarted.text: langchain for quick starts, langgraph for low-level control, or deepagents for long-running work.
Courses for building and testing agents.
